def: The earliest event in a merged timeline that differs from expected behaviour. Later errors are candidate consequences of it; debugging starts here, not at the loudest error.
An experiment whose outcome differs depending on which of two or more competing hypotheses is true, so running it eliminates at least one of them.
The number of commands completed per second. Meaningful only with the block size, read/write mix, access pattern and queue depth stated.
The maximum number of commands a submitter allows to be outstanding at once (for example fio's iodepth). Distinct from the NVMe queue size and from the in-flight depth actually achieved.
The high percentiles of a latency distribution (p99, p99.9, p99.99, maximum). Averages hide it; fan-out makes it dominate system behaviour.
L = λW: in a stable system the average number of items in the system equals their arrival (completion) rate times the average time each spends inside. Links outstanding commands, IOPS and latency.

The measured fraction of a defined space (requirements, normative statements, states, command fields, error paths, configurations, firmware code) exercised by tests. Each dimension misses what the others catch.
A test that applies invalid or out-of-contract stimulus and checks that the device detects and reports it as required and remains healthy.

Deliberately introducing controlled faults (corrupted or dropped packets, poisoned data, power loss, simulated error reports) to exercise detection and recovery paths. The method determines which layer's detection is really tested.
A test rerun after every change to confirm existing behaviour still works, including tests written from past bugs that check the failure mechanism.
The set of configurations (platform, link, MPS, kernel, firmware, format, power policy, and so on) under which tests run; usually reduced with pairwise selection and risk weighting.
The rule, model or reference data that decides whether an observed test outcome passes or fails.
In PCIe 6.0 and later Flit mode, the fixed 256-byte unit carrying TLP bytes, data-link information, CRC and forward error correction; replaces per-TLP framing and LCRC.
A measurement bias in closed-loop benchmarks: when the system stalls, the load generator submits less, so stalls are under-sampled and tail latency looks better than real users experience.
Bringing an SSD to a defined, representative state (typically purge, fill, then run the target workload to steady state) before measuring performance.
